key_insight: Physics-informed Vision Transformer frameworks estimate diffuse horizontal irradiance from scarce sky images, approaching the accuracy of a full-data ViT baseline.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce reliance on costly irradiance sensors for photovoltaic performance optimisation and solar energy forecasting.
method: Add calculated atmospheric parameters and cyclic time encodings without additional instrumentation.
Use predicted synthetic global horizontal irradiance as an input to refine diffuse irradiance estimates.
Process raw and overlay-enhanced sky images in parallel, using unsupervised, physics-informed cloud segmentation.
evidence_signal: On Chilbolton Observatory data, single-month training and temporally disjoint full-year testing yielded RMSE differences from a full-data ViT of 2–3 W/m² for the sequential framework and 1–6 W/m² for the dual-parallel framework.
watch_item: Validation is limited to one temperate-climate site; transfer to other climates and sky-camera setups remains unestablished.
paper_title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images
